newsitem.title: UK: LME key copper spread fails to narrow, zinc strong.
newsitem.headline: LME key copper spread fails to narrow, zinc strong.

text.p: Strong LME copper spreads kept the market buoyant on Monday afternoon and zinc hovered under fresh seven-year highs ahead of more gains, traders and analysts said.
The cash/three months backwardation widened slightly by the end of the afternoon kerb to $145/$150 from about $138/$148 on Friday.
The market had expected the spread to narrow by about $25 per day as tight dates drop out of the equation, but borrowing of August/threes on Monday propped it up, traders said.
The tomorrow/next day spread traded up to its LME-imposed limit of $24 per tonne earlier in the day.
"People who are short seem to be rolling forward their positions," said analyst Robin Bahr of broker Brandeis.
The shorts apparently are expecting a coming surplus to push prices down and allow them to close out the positions at a profit, he added.
The three months market, which has been virtually ignored recently in favour of cash and the spreads, extended its upward track to hit a high of $2,340 before ending the day $3 firmer at $2,319.
Stocks rose by 3,250 tonnes on Monday, which may signal that last week's big deliveries of 42,025 tonnes comprised several one-off lumps, Bahr said.
"It's hard to say, but maybe we'll see about 3,000 tonnes each day, a total of 15,000 tonnes this week."
Zinc stocks fell by a healthy 3,650 tonnes, helping prices to power up to hit a fresh peak since August 1990 at $1,540. It finished the kerb $6 firmer at $1,530.
The market's breathless advance despite overbought signals has defied forecasts of a pull-back.

"Zinc continues to surprise. We have all called for a correction and it hasn't come...Until there is a sign the market is turning you've got to stay long, the weight of money is too heavy," said Bahr.
Aluminium also pushed higher, peaking at $1,617 before profit-taking and possible producer activity trimmed gains. Prices ended $1.50 firmer at $1,609.
A steady erosion of stocks -- including a decline of 2,700 tonnes on Monday -- has supported the market but speculators have not been as active in aluminium as in zinc.
Resistance of $2,320, the high of July 3, and the 100-day moving average at $1,618, were temporarily capping the market, chartists said.
Nickel held in its $6,700-$6,900 range of the past few days, ending the kerb $50 higher at $6,790.
The market is indecisive, looking for direction after failing at the upper end of the range last week, traders said.
Tin dipped below $5,420 support to a fresh 2-1/3 year low of $5,400.
It ended the day at $5,410, a loss of $50, and traders said more losses were expected.
Lead was little changed at $647 versus $648/49 on Friday and alloy ended at $1,445/50, up slightly from $1,442/45.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
